title: Protocol for visualizing conditional interaction between transmembrane and cytoplasmic proteins
protocol: Seed cells based on the aim of your experiment.
SeedList the cells in a low-cell density condition such as 1.0 × 10^4 cells/well in a 24-well plate to inhibit the Hippo signal.
Ensure mycoplasma contamination is confirmed before starting the experiment and use mycoplasma-eliminated cells.
Sterilize cover slips by UV irradiation in a clean bench for 30–60 minutes (if collagen solution is sterilized, skip this step).
Wash the cover slips twice using a medium with antibiotics by gently shaking.
Seed cells on collagen-coated cover slips.
Culture cells at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Use MCF10A cells cultured in Mammary Epithelial Cell Growth Medium (MEGM) supplemented with penicillin and streptomycin instead of GA-1000.
Seed cells at a density of 6.25 × 10^3 cells/cm² for low-density condition or 6.25 × 10^4 cells/cm² as a positive control for Hippo signal activation.
Culture cells for 16 hours in a 5% CO2 environment at 37°C until the cells are well attached to the cover slips.
Prepare control samples for clustering of transmembrane proteins if available.
Select an antibody that recognizes the extracellular domain for cross-linking.
Decrease nonspecific signals as much as possible.
Check antibody specificity by immunofluorescence staining or immunoblotting.
Consider appropriate concentration for antibody dilution.
Consider incubation time and temperature for antibody dilution.
Choose antibodies (primary and secondary) made from different animal species than those used for PLA reaction.
Prepare the primary reaction solution containing the primary antibody.
Add the primary antibody to the culture medium at a final concentration of 0.5–20 μg/mL.
Add rat monoclonal anti-human CD44 antibody at a concentration of 10 μg/mL to MEGM with penicillin and streptomycin.
Incubate the cells for 90 min at 37°C in 5% CO2 with 1 mL of the primary reaction solution.
Wash the cells three times with culture medium or PBS.
Prepare a secondary reaction solution containing the appropriate secondary antibody.
Add the secondary antibody to the culture medium at a final concentration between 1–10 μg/mL, optimizing as necessary.
Incubate the cells for 60 min at 37°C in 5% CO2 with 1 mL of the secondary reaction solution.
Subject the cross-linked cells to immunofluorescence staining or PLA as required.
Rinse cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 1 mM MgCl2 at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Transfer cover slips into a new 12-well plate containing 1 mL of PBS with 1 mM MgCl2.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 1 mM MgCl2 for 5 min ×2 by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Fix the cells with 1 mL of 4% PFA/PBS for 15 min at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Wash cells with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Repeat step above once more.
Permeabilize cells with 1 mL of 0.25% TritonX-100/PBS for 10 min at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Wash cells with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Repeat step above once more.
Perform blocking using 1 mL of proper blocking solution for 60 min at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Wash cells with PBS containing 0.1% Tween 20 for 5 min by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Repeat step above once more.
Incubate cells overnight (12–16 h) at 4°C or for 60 min at room temperature (23°C–26°C) with a primary antibody.
Dilute the primary antibody in PBS or blocking solution as needed.
Tap off the PBS from the cover slips.
Transfer the cover slips into a humidified chamber.
Drop 50 μL of the antibody solution onto the cover slip.
Drop 5–10 μL of mount medium onto the slide glass.
Tap off PBS containing 0.1% tween 20 and transfer the cover slips into the humidified chamber.
Transfer the cover slips upside down onto the slide glass.
Gently wipe the extra amount of medium from around the cover slip.
Seal the edges of the cover slips using nail polish.
Prepare a secondary antibody solution by diluting a fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody in PBS or blocking solution.
Choose an appropriate fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody for your experiment.
Incubate the cells for 60 min with a secondary antibody solution at room temperature in the dark.
Tap off the PBS containing 0.1% tween 20.
Transfer the cover slips into the humidified chamber.
Drop 50 μL of the secondary antibody solution onto the cover slip.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 0.1% tween 20 for 10 min by gently shaking at room temperature in the dark.
Incubate the cells for 15 min with DAPI solution at room temperature in the dark.
Dilute the DAPI in PBS (1:1000).
Tap off the PBS containing 0.1% tween 20.
Transfer the cover slips into the humidified chamber.
Drop 50 μL of the DAPI solution onto the cover slip.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 0.1% tween 20 for 10 min by gently shaking at room temperature in the dark.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS for 10 min by gently shaking at room temperature in the dark.
Drop 5–10 μL of 90% glycerol/PBS onto the slide glass.
Tap off the PBS and transfer the cover slips upside down onto the slide glass.
Avoid the presence of air bubbles.
Wipe the extra amount of medium.
Seal the edges of the cover slips using nail polish.
Cure the nail polish before imaging to avoid damage to the objective.
Move to step 56 to take images.
Store the slides at 4°C in the dark for several days.
Rinse the cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 1 mM MgCl2 at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Transfer the cover slips into a new 12-well plate containing 1 mL of PBS with 1 mM MgCl2.
Wash the cells with PBS containing 1 mM MgCl2 for 5 min, repeating twice by gently shaking at room temperature.
Fix the cells with 1 mL of 4% PFA/PBS for 15 min at room temperature.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min, repeating twice by gently shaking at room temperature.
Permeabilize the cells with 1 mL of 0.25% TritonX-100/PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min ×2 by gently shaking at room temperature.
Perform blocking using 1 mL of proper blocking solution for 60 min at room temperature.
Wash the cells with PBS containing 0.1% tween 20 for 5 min ×2 by gently shaking at room temperature.
Incubate the cells overnight (12–16 h) at 4°C or for 60 min at room temperature with a primary antibody.
Dilute the primary antibody in the appropriate diluent.
If two primary antibodies are used, dilute them in the same diluent.
Tap off the PBS containing 0.1% tween 20 and transfer the cover slips into the humidified chamber.
Drop 50 μL of antibody solution onto the cover slip.
Transfer the cover slips into a 12-well plate.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 0.1% Tween 20 for 5 minutes at room temperature (23°C–26°C) by gently shaking.
Repeat step 2 once more.
Incubate the cells with DAPI solution in a humidified chamber at room temperature (23°C–26°C) in the dark for 15 minutes.
Dilute DAPI in PBS at a ratio of 1:1000.
Tap off the PBS containing 0.1% Tween 20.
Drop 50 μL of DAPI solution onto each cover slip.
Prepare PLA probe solution by mixing 8 μL of PLA probe MINUS, 8 μL of PLA probe PLUS, and 24 μL of antibody diluent for a total volume of 40 μL per reaction.
Dilute the PLUS and MINUS PLA probes at a ratio of 1:5 in Duolink Antibody Diluent or an appropriate diluent for your antibody combinations.
Allow the PLA probe mixture to sit at room temperature (23°C–26°C) for 20 minutes.
Transfer cover slips into a 12-well plate.
Wash cells with 1 mL of PBS containing 0.1% tween 20 for 5 minutes by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Incubate cells for 60 minutes with PLA probe solution at 37°C.
Tap off the PBS containing 0.1% tween 20.
Transfer cover slips into a humidified chamber and drop 40 μL of PLA probe solution onto the cover slip.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL of wash buffer A for 5 minutes each by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Prepare ligation-ligase solution by mixing 8 μL of 5× Ligation stock, 1 μL of ligase, and 31 μL of ddH2O.
Incubate cells for 30 minutes with the ligation-ligase solution at 37°C.
Tap off wash buffer A.
Transfer cover slips into a humidified chamber.
Drop 40 μL of ligation-ligase solution onto the cover slip.
Wash cells with 1 mL of wash buffer A for 5 min by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C).
Dilute the 5× Amplification stock 1:5 in ddH2O.
Add polymerase to the diluted amplification stock.
Prepare a 40 μL amplification-polymerase solution using the prepared components.
Incubate cells for 100 min with the amplification-polymerase solution at 37°C in the dark.
Tap off wash buffer A from cover slips.
Drop 40 μL of amplification-polymerase solution onto the cover slip.
Transfer cover slips into a humidified chamber after incubation.
Wash cells with 1 mL of wash buffer B for 5 min ×2 by gently shaking at room temperature (23°C–26°C) in the dark.
Rinse cells with 1 mL of diluted wash buffer B (1:100).
Drop 5-10 μL of 90% glycerol/PBS onto the slide glass.
Tap off diluted wash buffer B.
Let cover slips dry at room temperature (23°C–26°C) in the dark.
Transfer the cover slips upside down onto the slide glass.
Seal the edges of the cover slips using nail polish.
Store slides without decreasing the signal at 4°C in the dark for several days if needed.
Set imaging parameters of the confocal laser microscope.
Take images with excitation and emission filters compatible with the fluorophore and nuclear stain.
Treat cells with MEGM containing HMW-HA (1000 ng/mL) for 20 min as a positive control for CD44 clustering.
Treat cells with medium containing LMW-HA (1000 ng/mL) for 20 min as a negative control for CD44 clustering.
Seed MCF10A cells at a high density of 6.25 × 10^4 cells/cm² and culture for 16 h to activate the Hippo signaling pathway as a positive control.
Culture cells under indicated conditions and stain with anti-CD44 antibody (green).
Stain nuclei with DAPI (blue).
Take DIC images to visualize cell morphology optionally.
Stain cells with F-actin using fluorophore-conjugated phalloidin optionally.
Choose bright-field PLA detection reagent as an alternative option.
Perform hematoxylin staining for visualization of the nucleus when using the bright-field PLA detection reagent.
